title: Build a multiplier closure
description: Write a function `make_multiplier(factor)` that returns a new function. That returned function should take one argument `x` and return `x * factor`, remembering the `factor` it was created with even after `make_multiplier` has finished running.
hints: Instead of returning a number, this function needs to return another function, ready to be called later.
A function defined and returned from inside another function is called a closure — it keeps access to the variables of the scope it was created in, like `factor`.
Inside `make_multiplier`, define `def multiplier(x): return x * factor`, then `return multiplier` (without calling it) so the caller can invoke it later with their own `x`.
expected_behavior: Returns a function that, when later called with a number x, returns x * factor, where factor is fixed at the time make_multiplier was called.
explanation: `make_multiplier` defines a nested function `multiplier` that reads `factor` from the enclosing scope, and returns that function object itself (not its result). This is a closure: even after `make_multiplier` has returned, the function it produced still remembers the specific `factor` it was created with, which is why calling it later with `x` reproduces `x * factor`.
